title: Publish doctor host-version observation from @moe/daemon
description: Objective: make the landed Node-native doctor version observation callable through the public @moe/daemon package root so cross-host evidence can corroborate the real executing host and toolchain without a deep import or caller-selected host claim. Deliverable: curated root export and root-surface/type/loadability coverage for collectDoctorVersionReport plus its exact DoctorVersionReport type. NOT in scope: changing doctor report semantics, adding kernel/provider/evidence fields, or implementing the cross-host manifest. Current gap at HEAD 26ac640/8d9afb8: collectDoctorVersionReport exists at apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-version.node.ts:164 but @moe/daemon.collectDoctorVersionReport is undefined; scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs records this as doctor UNKNOWN. Consumer: task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/index.ts and apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts. These paths currently contain foreign WIP; do not begin until they are clean/committed and remeasure to avoid duplicate exports. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The bare @moe/daemon root exports collectDoctorVersionReport and DoctorVersionReport from the existing Node-native implementation without a deep import or duplicate collector.
Calling the root export derives platform, architecture, Node, pnpm, declared pins, and workspace component inventory from the running process/repository; no caller can select host identity.
The hand-written root runtime/type catalogue names the new surface exactly and its cardinality/list assertions cannot pass from a count-only change.
A plain-Node probe from apps/daemon loads the bare root and observes a callable collector; focused tests pin fail-closed behavior of the existing collector rather than reimplementing it.
task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a is recorded as the cross-host evidence consumer and fresh daemon test/typecheck gates exit 0.
taskRails: Do not start while apps/daemon/src/index.ts or index-surface.test.ts contains foreign WIP; remeasure committed HEAD first.
Publish the existing collector only; do not create a second doctor authority or accept caller-supplied platform/tool versions.
Keep the root below the 400-line split threshold, preserve exact curated exports, use TDD, and stage only the two owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — WRITE THE PROOFS FIRST, in `apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts`. Three distinct proofs, because the function and the type need different mechanisms.

PROOF A — RUNTIME CATALOGUE (DoD 3): add `["collectDoctorVersionReport", "function"]` to `EXPECTED_EXPORTS` in its alphabetical position (between `claimWork` and `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort`) and bump the length pin by one. The existing per-name kind and defined-ness checks then cover it.

PROOF B — THE TYPE, WHICH THE CATALOGUE CANNOT SEE (DoD 1). `EXPECTED_EXPORTS` checks `typeof value` and asserts defined-ness; a TYPE is `undefined` at runtime, so listing `DoctorVersionReport` there would FAIL rather than pin it. Prove it at COMPILE time instead — a type-only import from the bare `@moe/daemon` root plus an `expectTypeOf`-style assertion, or a compiled probe. Publishing the type and proving only the function meets half of DoD 1 while looking complete.

PROOF C — CALLABLE THROUGH THE BARE ROOT (DoD 4 and DoD 2). Import from the bare `@moe/daemon` specifier, CALL the collector and AWAIT it, then assert a field actually derived from the running process — the platform or the Node version — matches what this process reports. A `typeof x === "function"` check would pass for any stub and would prove neither callability nor DoD 2's "no caller can select host identity". Pass NOTHING and observe host truth come back; that absence of an argument is the point.

Do NOT re-cover the collector's fail-closed behaviour — doctor-version.node.test.ts already owns that (:288, :303, :333), and duplicating it creates a second place to maintain one claim.

All three fail until step 3.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SMALL TASK, TWO OWNED FILES, AND THE WORK IS ALMOST ENTIRELY IN GETTING THE PROOFS RIGHT. The publish itself is two lines. What decides whether it is worth anything is that the root-surface catalogue actually pins the new name, and that the TYPE export is proven by something other than the runtime catalogue — which cannot see it.

THE TYPE IS INVISIBLE TO THE RUNTIME CATALOGUE. `EXPECTED_EXPORTS` is a hand-written `[name, kind]` list checked with `typeof` (index-surface.test.ts:120-124). `DoctorVersionReport` is a TYPE: it vanishes at runtime, so adding it there would fail the defined-ness check, and omitting it means DoD 1's type half is unproven. The type needs a COMPILE-TIME proof — an `expectTypeOf`/type-only import in the test, or the packaging-style compiled probe. Two different mechanisms for two different exports; a plan that treats them alike gets one of them wrong.

THE COLLECTOR IS ASYNC. `export async function collectDoctorVersionReport(): Promise<DoctorVersionReport>` (doctor-version.node.ts:164). DoD 4 wants a plain-Node probe that "observes a callable collector" — a `typeof x === "function"` check passes for any stub, so the probe must actually CALL and AWAIT it and observe a real field derived from the running process. That is also what distinguishes DoD 2 ("no caller can select host identity") from a shape check.

PUBLISH, DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT (task rail 2). The root already has a doctor block at index.ts:159-174 re-exporting from `./recovery/doctor-commands.js`, plus `export type { DoctorVersionsReported } from "./recovery/doctor-version-contract.js";` at :175. So there is an established shape to join: the function comes from `./recovery/doctor-version.node.js`, and the type from `./recovery/doctor-version-contract.js` — the same module that line already pulls from. No new collector, no caller-supplied platform or tool versions.

REJECTED: adding fail-closed tests for the collector's own behaviour. DoD 4 says the focused tests "pin fail-closed behavior of the EXISTING collector rather than reimplementing it", and doctor-version.node.test.ts already covers it (:288, :303, :333). This task's tests prove REACHABILITY through the bare root; duplicating the behaviour coverage would create a second place to maintain the same claim.
